'''Kenneth O. Hill''' is a Mexican Canadian [[physicist]] who specializes in the field of [[photonics]]. In the late 1970s, he discovered the phenomenon of [[photosensitivity]] in [[optical fibre]] and has worked extensively in its applications.<ref name=CRCPhotosensitivity/><ref name=InventingCanada/> He first demonstrated [[Fiber Bragg gratings|fibre Bragg gratings]] and their applications in [[optical communications|optical communication]] and optical sensor systems.<ref name=CRCBraggGratings/> Further areas of his discovery and innovation include the phase mask technique for grating fabrication, fibre grating dispersion compensators, and wavelength selective fibre filters, [[multiplexing|multiplexers and demultiplexers]].<ref name=CAP/> This field of research has led to the ability to create high-speed fibre optic networks as well as many other communication applications that have revolutionized the [[telecommunication]]s industry.

==Early life and education==
Hill was born in 1939 in [[Guadalajara, Jalisco|Guadalajara]], [[Mexico]]. He attended the American elementary school in Guadalajara until high school, whereupon he attended [[Upper Canada College]] in [[Toronto]], Ontario, Canada.<ref name="InventingCanada" /> Hill pursued a B.Eng. (1963), M.Eng. (1965) as well as a Ph.D. in engineering physics (1968) from [[McMaster University]] in [[Hamilton, Ontario|Hamilton]], Ontario, Canada.<ref name=CAP/> He is also a [[Professional Engineer]] in the Province of [[Ontario]], Canada.<ref name=CRCBraggGratings/>

==Career==
Upon completing his Ph.D. in 1968, Hill worked for the Government of Canada's Defense Research Telecommunications Establishment (DRTE) as a research scientist.<ref name=InventingCanada/><ref name=CAP/><ref name=IEEE/> Later that year, the DRTE was converted to the [[Communications Research Centre Canada|Communications Research Centre]] (CRC). At CRC, he continued as a research scientist before working as a group leader in optical data storage and signal processing (1970–1975), manager of optical communications (1975–1985), director of optical communications (1985–1992) as well as principal scientist (1992–2000).<ref name=CAP/><ref name=IEEE/>

In 2000, Hill left CRC and was appointed to be the director of research at Nu-Wave Photonics/Zenastra Photonics Inc, operating in optical circuit and network design and manufacturing.<ref name=Nu-Wave/> In 2001, Hill joined OZ Optics Limited, a supplier of optical products for optical networks, as a part of their research team.<ref name=OZ/>

== Awards and honors ==
In 1991, Hill was elected to Fellowship in the [[Optical Society of America]] (OSA) for his efforts pertaining to fused fibre optical couplers, photosensitivity in fibre, novel fibre-based devices and nonlinear effects in fibre.<ref name=CAP/><ref name=OZ/> He was the 1995 recipient of the [[Manning Innovation Awards|Manning Principal Award]] for the discovery of photosensitivity in optical fibre as well as the many commercial applications his work led to.<ref name=InventingCanada/><ref name=CAP/><ref name=Manning/> At the 1996 Optical Fiber Communications Conference, Hill was awarded the [[John Tyndall Award]] sponsored by the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE), the [[IEEE Lasers and Electro-Optics Society|Lasers and Electro-Optics Society]] (LEOS) and the [[Optical Society of America]].<ref name=IEEE/><ref name=IEEE2/> The award was presented for the discovery of photosensitivity in optical fibres and its application to Bragg gratings used in device applications in optical communications and sensor systems."<ref name=IEEE/> In 1998, Hill was awarded the inaugural Medal for Outstanding Achievement in Applied Photonics from the [[Canadian Association of Physicists]] (CAP) and the National Optics Institute (INO).<ref name=CAP/> Hill was also awarded the Rank Prize in Optoelectronics in 2002 as one of four scientists recognized for creating and developing [[Fiber Bragg gratings|fibre Bragg gratings]].<ref name=Rank/>
